summary: MARS-X is an offline-first Mars exploration and navigation system with an Android app and 3D web interface. It uses NASA terrain data to help astronauts plan three types of routes: Safest, Quickest, and Most Scientific a detailed downloadable report can be produced. It also provides hazard detection, oxygen and water estimates, and GPS-free navigation using landmarks and compass directions. MARS-X helps astronauts explore Mars safely, save resources, and work independently without constant communication with Earth.
details:
What It Does & How It Works MARS-X is a 100% offline-first navigation and mission-planning app designed to help future astronauts safely plan and walk surface excursions in Jezero Crater, Mars—without needing GPS or internet. Explorers begin on an interactive 3D Mars globe before zooming into a high-resolution map of Jezero Crater layered with real NASA elevation, slope, surface roughness, and atmospheric pressure data. After tapping a start and end point, MARS-X’s pathfinding engine calculates three distinct routes in under two seconds: Safest, Quickest, and Most Scientific. Because Mars has no GPS satellites, MARS-X guides astronauts step-by-step using a Landmark Stepper with compass bearings, distances, 3D terrain flyovers, real Perseverance rover ground photos, and an emergency 3-landmark triangulation "I'm Lost" Re-Anchor tool.
Tools, Languages & Software Used-
Data Pipeline: Python, GDAL, and NumPy (to compress a 1.2 GB NASA HiRISE terrain GeoTIFF into an 18.2 KB offline binary grid).
Mobile & Web Apps: Flutter (Dart), Riverpod, SQLite, and PDF export for the offline Android APK paired with React 19, TypeScript, Vite, and Three.js for the 3D mission-control web suite.
NASA & USGS Datasets: MRO HiRISE DTM, MGS MOLA topography, USGS Viking MDIM 2.1 mosaic, and Mars 2020 Perseverance Mastcam-Z/MEDA data.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered-
Creative GPS-Free Design: Instead of relying on satellites, we treated the lack of GPS as a core design feature—building visual landmark dead-reckoning and 3-point triangulation directly into the user interface.
Astronaut Safety & Human Factors: We modeled Martian gravity (3.721m/s^2), steep (25 degree) cliff cutoffs, mandatory rest stopscapping scientific detours at 1.5 times the quickest distance.
Scientific Honesty: Every metric is strictly labeled as OBSERVED, DERIVED, MODELED, or SIMULATED so astronauts never confuse simulated estimates with direct sensor measurements.
